newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian senator blames office for claims.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian senator blames office for claims.

text.p: Key Australian independent senator Mal Colston on Monday conceded he had claimed travelling allowance to which he was not entitled but blamed the error on his office.

"My investigations have discovered that the inadequate bookkeeping systems in my office led to administrative errors on the part of my staff which caused the overpayments," Colston said in a written response to an administrative inquiry that discovered the excess claims.
He had refunded the money he had mistakenly claimed, he said.

Excess travel claims are one of several accusations of dishonesty that have been levelled against Colston, who defected from the Labor opposition in August and has since supplied a crucial vote needed to get the government's contentious legislation through parliament.
On Monday Senate President Margaret Reid published the result of the inquiry into the expense claims together with the senator's response to it.
Senate officials had checked Colston's travel claims for nights in Canberra against airline and government car records, the report showed.
The officials found 24 occasions on which Colston claimed to have been in Canberra but appeared not to have been there.
Colston responded that of the A$6,295 alleged excess payments, he had actually been overpaid A$5,730 due to poor bookkeeping. The officials were mistaken about the rest.

"The reports that you have tabled today contain irrefutable documentary evidence that while Senator Colston was claiming travel allowance for being in one place he was actually in another place," Labor opposition senator John Faulkner told Reid in the Senate.
But Government Senate Leader Robert Hill backed Colston's explanation against the Labor's disbelief and accused the opposition of trying to punish the senator for his defection.
Opposition senator Robert Ray called for further inquiries into the travel allowances.
